narrative.overview:
ANSI keeps the terminal’s functional color and precise machine values while giving people readable titles and plain-language help. The visual register is calm, direct and practical: glance, find the state that needs attention, act on one row, leave.

Both grounds are first-class. Structure comes from type, spacing and rules rather than decorative surfaces. The recorded world applies to the operator web app, not the terminal dashboard or marketing website.
keyCharacteristics: Two calm grounds with state-specific inks.
Human language in sans; machine values in mono.
Title-led ruled rows, inline answers and one confirmation dialog.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are equal supported grounds. Use the matching palette as a whole; never transplant an ink from the other ground.

rules.name: The Color Is State Rule
rules.body: Green marks done or running, amber marks provisional progress, retries, held work and consent, teal marks the current step and live interaction, blue identifies tickets and links, red marks blocked or failed, and slack marks pending. Status and step words carry meaning alongside color.

rules.name: The Semantic Type Rule
rules.body: Use Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for titles, captions, questions and explanatory prose. Use JetBrains Mono for ticket ids, slugs, steps, durations, repository identities, codes and other machine values.

rules.name: The Glyph Rule
rules.body: Retain the textual step marks [x], [>], [~], [ ] and their accessible state names. Existing text controls may use menu or close glyphs; never introduce an icon set or emoji.

rules.name: The Title First Rule
rules.body: The readable ticket title is the primary row text; use the slug when no title exists. Keep identity, status, slug and steps visible without opening detail.

rules.name: The Flowing Document Rule
rules.body: The browser document owns scrolling. Masthead, tabs, controls, rows and pages remain in ordinary flow at natural height, without pinned content or nested scrolling panels. Long lists load their next page as the reader nears the end. The account and project menus are the small anchored overlay exceptions, full-width on phones, and the confirmation dialog is the one modal.

rules.name: The Square Rules Rule
rules.body: Use square corners, one-pixel structural rules and thin outlined controls. No shadows, gradients, rounded pills or filled status badges.

rules.name: The Sign-off Rule
rules.body: Reserve a bordered sign-off region for a human decision. Escalation uses red question and border on red wash with plain explanatory copy; merge consent uses amber on the plain ground, never on the well.

dos: Do choose the palette for the active ground and preserve text contrast of at least 4.5:1.
Do explain what an escalation means and what answering does.
Do keep state words and step marks beside their color.
Do confirm destructive actions in the confirmation dialog and show acknowledged durable state.
donts: Don’t place amber text on the inset well or red wash; use the plain ground.
Don’t add shadows, gradients, pills, icon sets or emoji.
Don’t replace the build or ticket page with a drawer, modal or in-place expansion; the confirmation dialog is the only modal.
Don’t invent page numbers or decide a new app title; both remain human decisions.
